findings.summary: Drama fact names are rendered as data cells instead of row headers.
findings.consequence: Screen-reader table navigation cannot associate each fact value with its label as a row header, so the key-value facts are less understandable when navigating by cell.
findings.evidence: The drama facts table renders both the label and value with `<td>` cells: line 287 emits `{{ dramaLabels[fact.key] }}` in a `td`, and line 288 emits the value in another `td`. This is a row-label/value table, so the first cell carries header semantics for the row.
findings.recommendation: Render the label cell as `{{ dramaLabels[fact.key] }}` and keep the value as `{{ fact.value }}`.

findings.summary: Errata expand/collapse controls use anchors as buttons.
findings.consequence: The controls are not links and rely on manually recreated button semantics; native button behavior, form semantics, and assistive-technology expectations would be simpler and more robust with a real button element.
findings.evidence: The `Visa fler` control starts as an `<a>` at line 351 with `role="button"`, `tabindex="0"`, and manual Enter/Space handlers. The `Visa färre` control repeats the same pattern at line 360.
findings.recommendation: Use `<button type="button" class="toggle sc" @click="toggleErrata">` for both controls and remove the role, tabindex, and manual keydown handlers.
